summary: Toshifumi Goto is an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD from the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg in 1982. He held professorships at Osaka University and Tohoku University (attested 2003-2012).
Toshihide Mori is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. Mori held a post as a part-time lecturer at Chikushi Jogakuen Junior College (attested 1995).

Toshihiko Izutsu (1914-1993) worked in philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies, studying at Keio University (~1934-1937) and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Keio University (~1937-1969), McGill University (~1969-1975), and Komazawa University (attested 1988).

Toshihiko Kimura is an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1959-1963). He held posts at Tokai Gakuin University (attested 1981-1987), Shitennoji University (~1988), and Tohoku University.
Toshihiro Wada is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Vashishtha Narayan Jha in 1981. He served on the faculty at Nagoya University from ~1988 to 2020.

Toshiichi Endo is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed undergraduate studies at the University of Kelaniya and a doctoral thesis at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies in 1995. He was a professor at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2016).

Toshikazu Watanabe is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2011), the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2015-2019), and Kokugakuin University (2018).

Toshiki Osada is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Hokkaido University (~1973-1977). He served at the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature (~2003-2020) and Kyoto University of the Arts (~2020).

Toshinori Ochiai is a Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology scholar. He held posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996-2019), Kacho Junior College (attested 2001), and the Research Institute of Old Japanese Manuscripts of Buddhist Scriptures (~2004).
Toshio Ando (1909-1973) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1930-1934). He held posts at Doho University (~1950-1957) and Otani University (~1957-1973).

Toshio Horiuchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who earned his PhD from the University of Tokyo (~2004-2012). He held research posts at Toyo University (attested 2015-2020) and Zhejiang University (~2018).

Toshio Nagahiro (1905-1990) specialized in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, studying at Kyoto University (~1925-1928). He held professorships at Kyoto University (~1952-1969) and Kyoto Tachibana University (~1969-1978).
Toshio Sako is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikido Takasaki and Yasunori Ejima, and at Columbia University under Alex Wayman.

Toshio Yamazaki (1916-1994) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1961-1977), Chuo University (~1977-1987), Tokyo Institute of Technology, and Hannan University.
Toshiya Unebe is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Musashi Tachikawa. He served as an associate professor at Nagoya University (attested 2009).
Totsudo Kato (1870-1949) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied under Enryo Inoue (~1889-1893) and Seiran Ouchi, and later held a post at Nihon University.

Tou-hui Fok (1940-2018) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at New Asia College, New Asia Institute, CUHK, and Otani University. He held a lecturing post at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~1972-1986).
Tracy Franz is a Buddhist studies scholar who held teaching posts at Dalhousie University and Shokei University (both attested 2018).

Travis L. Smith is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at UC Berkeley and earned a PhD from Columbia University in 2007. Smith has held posts at Barnard College and the University of Florida (attested 2012).
Trent Walker is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed a PhD at the University of California, Berkeley under doctoral supervisor Alexander von Rospatt.
